fanoutqa_027105.t: Alcohol and cancer :: Recommended maximum alcohol intake :: chunk_0029
fanoutqa_027105.x:
Alcohol and cancer :: Recommended maximum alcohol intake :: chunk_0029
Main article: [Alcohol consumption recommendations](/wiki/Alcohol_consumption_recommendations "Alcohol consumption recommendations")

As outlined above, there is no recommended alcohol intake with respect to cancer risk alone as it varies with each individual cancer. See [Alcohol consumption recommendations](/wiki/Alcohol_consumption_recommendations "Alcohol consumption recommendations") for a list of governments' guidances on alcohol intake which, for a healthy man, range from 140–280g per week.

One meta-analysis suggests that risks of cancers may start below the recommended levels. "Risk increased significantly for drinkers, compared with non-drinkers, beginning at an intake of 25 g (< 2 standard drinks) per day for the following: cancers of the oral cavity and pharynx (relative risk, RR, 1.9), esophagus (RR 1.4), larynx (RR 1.4), breast (RR 1.3), liver (RR 1.2), colon (RR 1.1), and rectum (RR 1.1)"[[185]](#cite_note-185)[[186]](#cite_note-186)

World Cancer Research Fund recommends that people aim to limit consumption to less than two drinks a day for a man and less than one drink a day for a woman. It defines a "drink" as containing about 10–15 grams of ethanol.[[187]](#cite_note-187)

India :: Culture :: Music :: chunk_0038
Main article: [Music of India](/wiki/Music_of_India "Music of India")

India contains a wide array of musical practices, including many different [folk musics](/wiki/Indian_folk_music "Indian folk music") from different regions. [Indian classical music](/wiki/Indian_classical_music "Indian classical music") has Vedic origins, and split in the 13th century into the two main traditions of [Hindustani](/wiki/Hindustani_classical_music "Hindustani classical music") and [Carnatic](/wiki/Carnatic_music "Carnatic music") music. Hindustani is associated with North India and is more [improvisational](/wiki/Musical_improvisation "Musical improvisation"), featuring instruments such as the [sitar](/wiki/Sitar "Sitar") and [tabla](/wiki/Tabla "Tabla"), and Carnatic is South Indian and more focused on written [compositions](/wiki/Musical_composition "Musical composition") such as the *[kriti](/wiki/Kriti_(music) "Kriti (music)")*, while both styles contain common elements such as the [raga](/wiki/Raga "Raga") melodic framework and [tala](/wiki/Tala_(music) "Tala (music)") rhythmic meter.[[405]](#cite_note-431) Indian music has influenced western genres, notably [rock](/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music") and [jazz](/wiki/Jazz "Jazz") musicians during the [1960s counterculture](/wiki/Counterculture_of_the_1960s "Counterculture of the 1960s").[[406]](#cite_note-432)

[Filmi](/wiki/Filmi "Filmi") is music written for [Indian cinema](/wiki/Cinema_of_India "Cinema of India"), generally composed by [music directors](/wiki/List_of_Indian_film_music_directors "List of Indian film music directors") and sung by [playback singers](/wiki/Playback_singers "Playback singers"). Modern [Indian pop](/wiki/Indian_pop "Indian pop") takes influences from classical, folk, and western pop music.[[407]](#cite_note-433)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/Babe_Ruth_by_Paul_Thompson%2C_1920.jpg/250px-Babe_Ruth_by_Paul_Thompson%2C_1920.jpg)](/wiki/File:Babe_Ruth_by_Paul_Thompson,_1920.jpg)

[Babe Ruth](/wiki/Babe_Ruth "Babe Ruth"), often considered the greatest baseball player of all time, in 1920

Baseball's popularity increased in the 1920s and 1930s. The 1920 season was notable for the death of [Ray Chapman](/wiki/Ray_Chapman "Ray Chapman") of the [Cleveland Indians](/wiki/Cleveland_Indians "Cleveland Indians"). Chapman, who was struck in the head by a pitch and died a few hours later, became the only MLB player to die of an on-field injury.[[52]](#cite_note-52) Both leagues quickly began to require the use of new, white baseballs whenever a ball became scuffed or dirty, helping bring the "dead-ball" era to an end.

The following year, the [New York Yankees](/wiki/New_York_Yankees "New York Yankees") made their first World Series appearance.[[53]](#cite_note-Plaque-53) By the end of the 1930s, the team had appeared in 11 World Series, winning eight of them.[[54]](#cite_note-BR-54) Yankees slugger [Babe Ruth](/wiki/Babe_Ruth "Babe Ruth") had set the single-season home run record in 1927, hitting 60 home runs; breaking his own record of 29 home runs.[[55]](#cite_note-Swat-55)

Impacted negatively by the [Great Depression](/wiki/Great_Depression_in_the_United_States "Great Depression in the United States"), baseball's popularity had begun a downward turn in the early 1930s. By 1932, only two MLB teams turned a profit. Attendance had fallen, due at least in part to a 10% federal amusement tax added to baseball ticket prices. Baseball owners cut their [rosters](/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_rosters "Major League Baseball rosters") from 25 men to 23, and even the best players took pay cuts. Go is a popular game in South Korea, China, and Japan. This match was watched and analyzed by millions of people worldwide.[[69]](#cite_note-latimes_milestone-69) Many top Go players characterized AlphaGo's unorthodox plays as seemingly-questionable moves that initially befuddled onlookers but made sense in hindsight:[[73]](#cite_note-cbc_sweeps-73) "All but the very best Go players craft their style by imitating top players. AlphaGo seems to have totally original moves it creates itself."[[69]](#cite_note-latimes_milestone-69) AlphaGo appeared to have unexpectedly become much stronger, even when compared with its October 2015 match against Fan Hui[[81]](#cite_note-81) where a computer had beaten a Go professional for the first time without the advantage of a handicap.[[82]](#cite_note-nature_react-82)

China's number one player, [Ke Jie](/wiki/Ke_Jie "Ke Jie"), who was at the time the top-ranked player worldwide, initially claimed that he would be able to beat AlphaGo, but declined to play against it for fear that it would "copy my style".[[83]](#cite_note-83) As the matches progressed, Ke Jie went back and forth, stating that "it is highly likely that I (could) lose" after analyzing the first three matches,[[84]](#cite_note-84) but regaining confidence after the fourth match.[[85]](#cite_note-85) In the end, Ke Jie [played Alpha Go](/wiki/AlphaGo_versus_Ke_Jie "AlphaGo versus Ke Jie") the next year and was defeated in three games.

Toby Manning, the referee of AlphaGo's match against Fan Hui, and Hajin Lee, secretary general of the [International Go Federation](/wiki/International_Go_Federation "International Go Federation"), both reason that in the future, Go players will get help from computers to learn what they have done wrong in games and improve their skills.[[82]](#cite_note-nature_react-82)

**Spanish** (*español*) or **Castilian** (*castellano*) is a [Romance language](/wiki/Romance_languages "Romance languages") of the [Indo-European language family](/wiki/Indo-European_languages "Indo-European languages") that evolved from the [Vulgar Latin](/wiki/Vulgar_Latin "Vulgar Latin") spoken on the [Iberian Peninsula](/wiki/Iberian_Peninsula "Iberian Peninsula") of [Europe](/wiki/Europe "Europe"). It originated in the [Kingdom of Castile](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Castile "Kingdom of Castile"), a historical kingdom in north-central [Spain](/wiki/Spain "Spain").[[4]](#cite_note-4) Today, it is a [global language](/wiki/World_language "World language") with 519 million native speakers, mainly in the [Americas](/wiki/Americas "Americas") and Spain, and about 636 million speakers total, including second-language speakers. Spanish is the official language of [20 countries](/wiki/List_of_countries_where_Spanish_is_an_official_language "List of countries where Spanish is an official language"), as well as one of the [six official languages](/wiki/Official_languages_of_the_United_Nations "Official languages of the United Nations") of the [United Nations](/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations").[[5]](#cite_note-un1-5)[[6]](#cite_note-6) Spanish is the world's [second-most spoken native language](/wiki/List_of_languages_by_number_of_native_speakers "List of languages by number of native speakers") after [Mandarin Chinese](/wiki/Mandarin_Chinese "Mandarin Chinese");[[7]](#cite_note-size-7)[[8]](#cite_note-8) the world's [fourth-most spoken language](/wiki/List_of_languages_by_total_number_of_speakers "List of languages by total number of speakers") overall after [English](/wiki/English_language "English language"), Mandarin Chinese, and [Hindustani](/wiki/Hindustani_language "Hindustani language") ([Hindi](/wiki/Hindi "Hindi")-[Urdu](/wiki/Urdu "Urdu")); and the world's most widely spoken Romance language. The relationship between the university and the city of [Cambridge](/wiki/Cambridge "Cambridge") has sometimes been uneasy. The phrase [town and gown](/wiki/Town_and_gown "Town and gown") continues to be employed to distinguish between Cambridge residents (town) and University of Cambridge students (gown), who historically wore [academical dress](/wiki/Academic_dress "Academic dress"). Ferocious rivalry between Cambridge's residents and university students have periodically erupted over the centuries. During the [Peasants' Revolt](/wiki/Peasants%27_Revolt "Peasants' Revolt") of 1381, strong clashes led to attacks and [looting](/wiki/Looting "Looting") of university properties as locals contested the privileges granted by the British government to the University of Cambridge's academic staff. Residents burned university property in [Market Square](/wiki/Market_Hill,_Cambridge "Market Hill, Cambridge") to the famed rallying cry "[Away with the learning of clerks, away with it!](/wiki/Away_with_the_learning_of_clerks,_away_with_it! "Away with the learning of clerks, away with it!")".[[48]](#cite_note-49) Following these events, the [University of Cambridge's Chancellor](/wiki/List_of_chancellors_of_the_University_of_Cambridge "List of chancellors of the University of Cambridge") was given special powers allowing him to prosecute criminals and reestablish order in the city. Attempts at reconciliation between the city's residents and students followed; in the 16th century, agreements were signed to improve the quality of streets and student accommodation around the city. Kennedy") in 1963. He was the [youngest](/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_the_United_States_by_age "List of presidents of the United States by age") person [elected](/wiki/United_States_presidential_election "United States presidential election") president, at 43 years,[[a]](#cite_note-2) and the first [Catholic](/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church") president. Kennedy served at the height of the [Cold War](/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War"), and the majority of his foreign policy concerned relations with the [Soviet Union](/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") and [Cuba](/wiki/Cuba "Cuba"). A member of the [Democratic Party](/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)"), Kennedy represented [Massachusetts](/wiki/Massachusetts "Massachusetts") in both houses of the [United States Congress](/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress") before his presidency.

Born into the prominent [Kennedy family](/wiki/Kennedy_family "Kennedy family") in [Brookline, Massachusetts](/wiki/Brookline,_Massachusetts "Brookline, Massachusetts"), Kennedy graduated from [Harvard University](/wiki/Harvard_University "Harvard University") in 1940, joining the [U.S. Naval Reserve](/wiki/U.S._Naval_Reserve "U.S. Naval Reserve") the following year. Christopher Maurice Brown[[40]](#cite_note-the_vogue-41) was born on May 5, 1989,[[41]](#cite_note-Allmusic-42) in [Tappahannock, Virginia](/wiki/Tappahannock,_Virginia "Tappahannock, Virginia"),[[42]](#cite_note-theg-43) to Joyce Hawkins, a former [day care](/wiki/Day_care "Day care") center director, and Clinton Brown,[[43]](#cite_note-spiral-44) a [corrections officer](/wiki/Corrections_officer "Corrections officer") at a local prison.[[44]](#cite_note-Times_Online-45)[[45]](#cite_note-NME-46) He has an older sister, Lytrell Bundy,[[46]](#cite_note-Biography_Today-47) a bank employee.[[44]](#cite_note-Times_Online-45) Music was always present in Brown's life beginning in his childhood. He would listen to [soul](/wiki/Soul_music "Soul music") albums that his parents owned,[[45]](#cite_note-NME-46) and eventually began to show interest in the [hip-hop](/wiki/Hip-hop "Hip-hop") scene.[[41]](#cite_note-Allmusic-42)

His parents had divorced when he was 6 years old,[[43]](#cite_note-spiral-44) and his mother's boyfriend[[b]](#cite_note-48) terrified him by subjecting her to [domestic violence](/wiki/Domestic_violence "Domestic violence").[[47]](#cite_note-49) In a 2017 self-documentary film, *[Welcome to My Life](/wiki/Welcome_to_My_Life_(film) "Welcome to My Life (film)")*, Brown recalls the couple's abusive relationship. Brown said that when he was six, his mother's partner shot himself in the head, but did not die. The gunshot blinded him, the physical impairment only adding to his rage. Donnelle vented his anger and frustration on Brown's mother. "I had to hear my mom get beat up every night. I'd pee on myself, just scared to even walk out into the hallway, because I didn't want to see nothing".[[48]](#cite_note-salon-50)

Brown taught himself to sing and dance at a young age and often cites [Michael Jackson](/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson") as his inspiration.[[44]](#cite_note-Times_Online-45)

The film has received various awards and nominations. The film was considered to be one of the best films of the year by the [National Board of Review](/wiki/National_Board_of_Review "National Board of Review"), making it only the second non-English film ever to make it to the list.[[398]](#cite_note-400) *RRR* became the third Indian film and first Telugu film to receive nominations at the [Golden Globe Awards](/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards"). It was nominated for [Best Foreign Language Film](/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Foreign_Language_Film "Golden Globe Award for Best Foreign Language Film"), and [Best Original Song](/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song") for "[Naatu Naatu](/wiki/Naatu_Naatu "Naatu Naatu")", winning the latter, made the song the first Asian nomination to win the award.[[17]](#cite_note-:21-19)[[18]](#cite_note-Davis-20) The song "Naatu Naatu" also won the Academy Award for [Best Original Song](/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Academy Award for Best Original Song") at the [95th Academy Awards](/wiki/95th_Academy_Awards "95th Academy Awards"), making it the first and only Indian song to win at the Oscars.[[399]](#cite_note-401)
